19515.step: {"blocks":[{"key":"cfrq5","text":"Filter sterilize extraction buffer using a 0.22 uM filter attached to a syringe.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"avs2i","text":"For fresh tissue: ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[{"style":"bold","offset":0,"length":18}],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"8st1o","text":"Place sample into a sterile glass homogenizer.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"84l2s","text":"Add 0.375 mL of extraction buffer, and gently homogenise the tissue. ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"7ielc","text":"","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"ann0a","text":"For frozen homogenized tissue samples (in 1.5 mL tubes): ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[{"style":"bold","offset":0,"length":57}],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"6n948","text":"Add 0.375 mL of the extraction buffer to the tube. ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"fivbb","text":"Pour buffer and sample into homogeniser and homogenise. ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"e0jp0","text":"Use 1000 µL pipette to transfer everything back into original tube.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"2u6dk","text":"","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"7970b","text":"For water samples on filter paper (in 1.5 mL tubes): ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[{"style":"bold","offset":0,"length":53}],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"47t3a","text":"Add 0.375 mL of the extraction buffer to the tube. ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"5da05","text":"You may want to add more to cover all filter paper.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"366v4","text":"","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"594q3","text":"Briefly vortex and incubate at 37°C using an incubator or heat block for 30 min. This allows the lysozyme to digest bacterial cell walls - particularly gram positive cells which have a high proportion of peptidoglycan. ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"ctpsg","text":"Add 10 µL of 20 mg/mL Proteinase K to digest proteins. The 1% SDS in the solution enhances proteinase K activity.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}
{"blocks":[{"key":"bmhis","text":"Add ~50 mg of sterile glass beads.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"593jf","text":"Process in Tissue Lyser at max speed (30 shakes/s) for 30 seconds to break apart the cells.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}
{"blocks":[{"key":"5lva3","text":"Incubate in 65°C incubator/heat block for 1 hour.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}
{"blocks":[{"key":"e784o","text":"Remove samples and change setting to 37°C.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}
{"blocks":[{"key":"5dfgr","text":"Add 90 µL of 5 M KOAc.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}
{"blocks":[{"key":"bh7ia","text":"Incubate on ice for 30 minutes.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}
{"blocks":[{"key":"6f33m","text":"Centrifuge at 15000xg for 15 minutes at 4°C (tab up).","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"3l6c4","text":"Transfer supernatant to a new 1.5 mL tube. If much floating material remains, re-spin for 15 minutes (avoid the pelleted protein).","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"afoo5","text":"Add 5 µL of 10 mg/mL RNase-A to supernatant in new tube and incubate @ 37°C in incubator/heat block for 30 minutes (leave heat block on afterwards).","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}
{"blocks":[{"key":"8m16i","text":"Add 500 µL of isopropanol to precipitate.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}
{"blocks":[{"key":"8a3ht","text":"Mix gently and let stand for 15 minutes at room temperature.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}
{"blocks":[{"key":"6pdm","text":"Centrifuge at 15000xg for 15 minutes at 4°C (tab up).","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"d46n6","text":"Carefully remove supernatant with pipette (position the tip opposite the tab side). Its okay to leave some supernatant behind. Don’t worry if you don’t see a pellet.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"cijic","text":"Add 150 µL of 70% ethanol to wash the DNA (apply against the tab side), and centrifuge at 15000xg for 2 mins (tab up) at 4°C.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"cq4au","text":"Carefully remove all supernatant with pipette (position tip opposite the tab side).","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"7sq93","text":"Air-dry by putting the tubes in the 37˚C block from the heat block and leaving them in the laminar flow for ≥15 mins with the lids open to evaporate the alcohol.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}
{"blocks":[{"key":"4td1f","text":"Add 50 µL of sterile water. Vortex then centrifuge for ~10 seconds.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"9d1na","text":"Leave overnight at 4°C to resuspend the DNA. DNA can be stored long term at -20°C.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

description: {"blocks":[{"key":"1kfk","text":"This protocol details the steps after DNA extraction to prepare a sequencing library for Illumina MiSeq sequencing at The Walter and Eliza Hall Institute (WEHI) with Stephen Wilcox. Stephen must be contacted (swilcox@wehi.edu.au) so that you can collect NGS beads and indexing primers. ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}
guidelines: {"blocks":[{"key":"2b6m3","text":"Primers with Illumina Nextera adapters designed at the Walter and Eliza Hall Institute (WEHI), Melbourne, Australia, targeting the V5-V6 regions of the bacterial 16S rRNA genes: ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[{"style":"UNDERLINE","offset":13,"length":25}],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"2ahmd","text":"784F [5ʹ GTGACCTATGAACTCAGGAGTCAGGATTAGATACCCTGGTA 3ʹ]; ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[{"style":"UNDERLINE","offset":9,"length":22}],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"cqkbh","text":"1061R [5ʹ CTGAGACTTGCACATCGCAGCCRRCACGAGCTGACGAC3ʹ] (Andersson et al., 2008)","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[{"style":"UNDERLINE","offset":10,"length":21}],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"4cuv9","text":"or the internal transcribed spacer 2 (ITS2) region of the Symbiodiniaceae rRNA gene:","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"4bid9","text":"Sym_Var_5.8S2 [5’ GTGACCTATGAACTCAGGAGTCGAATTGCAGAACTCCGTGAACC 3’] (Hume et al., 2015); ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[{"style":"UNDERLINE","offset":18,"length":22}],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"dhfn3","text":"Sym_Var_Rev [5’ CTGAGACTTGCACATCGCAGCCGGGTTCWCTTGTYTGACTTCATGC 3’] (Hume et al., 2013).","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[{"style":"UNDERLINE","offset":16,"length":21}],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"c51i7","text":"Prepare your PCR master mix (MM) by multiplying the number of samples you have (+ a few extra) with the \"per sample\" volume listed below for your 2x polymerase master mix, primers, and milli-Q water. For example, if I had 85 samples, I would make enough MM for 100. Add those volumes into a reservoir/boat. You can mix by gently sliding the mixture side to side - do not excessively pipet. You should have already tested your chosen polymerase with a trial PCR. {"blocks":[{"key":"86uh9","text":"Transfer 51 ul of your PCR MM to each well. Then add 4 ul of the respective sample to your well. You will need at least three PCR negatives (no sample) for data analysis and you should also include a minimum of 3 extraction blanks, and a mock community sample. Seal the plate(s) with an aluminum seal, vortex, and centrifuge.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"bu6nl","text":"Carefully remove the seal, and, keeping the same sample positions, pipet 3x 15 µL to new plates. You will now have four plates for each sample - the 3x 15 µL plates and 1x 10 µL. The 10 µL plate will be run for 35 cycles in PCR as a test to make sure that all samples have amplified. The 3x 15 µL plates will each go through the thermocycler for 18 cycles. Plates should be sealed with the clear PCR seal and centrifuged prior to running PCR.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"j34l","text":"","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"1qsc8","text":"MyTaq polymerase OH PCR settings: 1 cycle × 95°C for 3 min; 18 or 35 cycles × 95°C for 15 s, 55°C* for 30 s, and 72°C for 30 s; 1 cycle × 72°C for 7 min; hold at 4°C","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[{"style":"bold","offset":60,"length":8}],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"fll8f","text":"","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"ct9kc","text":"Qiagen polymerase OH PCR settings: 1 cycle × 95°C for 10 min; 18 or 35 cycles × 95°C for 30 s, 55°C* for 60 s, and 72°C for 30 s; 1 cycle × 72°C for 7 min; hold at 4°C.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[{"style":"bold","offset":62,"length":8}],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"dbor1","text":"","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"78q3e","text":"*55°C works well for 16S (784f/1061r; 515f/806r) and ITS2 (Sym_Var_5.8S2/Sym_Var_Rev), but you may need to adjust these for your PCR settings","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"fmrho","text":"Run a gel (1% agarose with TAE buffer) at 125 V for 30 min to visualize bands in the 35 cycle plate only. Once a band is confirmed, the 3x 15 µL reactions are pooled into one plate (total 45 µL volume). This is your OH PCR product. Quantifying DNA concentration is not necessary. Plates can be stored at -20°C for several months. ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[{"style":"bold","offset":85,"length":21}],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}
{"blocks":[{"key":"3mku5","text":"Transfer 20 µL of OH PCR product to a new plate. ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"2saab","text":"Add 20 µL (1:1 ratio) of NGS beads (collected from WEHI) using a multichannel pipet – seal the plate with an aluminum seal and mix well on a vortex. Do a brief (5-10s) centrifugation and wait 5 mins for beads to bind DNA. (total 40 µL) The beads should be evenly distributed in the solution and not concentrated in the bottom of the well.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"bknna","text":"Put plate onto magnetic rack and wait until you can see beads attaching to the side of the wells.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"fp5f7","text":" ","type":"atomic","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[{"key":0,"offset":0,"length":1}],"data":{}},{"key":"7i8yl","text":"This is the type of magnetic rack that our lab group prefers.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":null,"entityRanges":null,"data":{}},{"key":"19lgm","text":"","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{"0":{"type":"image","mutability":"","data":{"guid":"620A8810341F11EE9D4302C0B41BC903","height":216,"id":1412511,"is_video":false,"legend":"{\"blocks\":null,\"entityMap\":null}","mime":"image/png","original_name":"image.png","placeholder":"https://content.protocols.io/files/drtr2rv6.jpg","source":"https://content.protocols.io/files/bmdn92rv6.jpg","type":1,"webp_placeholder":"https://s3.amazonaws.com/protocols-files/files/drtq2rv6.webp","webp_source":"https://content.protocols.io/files/bmdn82rv6.webp","width":234}}}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"bcgkc","text":"Remove seal. Carefully remove supernatant – be careful not to disturb the beads.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"d0ukc","text":"Gently add 150 µL of 70% ethanol and pipette up and down gently. Remove ethanol.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"b4cua","text":"Repeat step 10 and take care to remove as much ethanol as possible without disturbing the pellets. To do this you can go through each well with a 10 µL pipet to collect the residual ethanol.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"b232j","text":"Let plate air dry – can place plate on heat block to speed up excess ethanol evaporation. When beads are dry the pellets will have a dry flakey appearance.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"cglme","text":"Add 40 µL of nuclease free H2O, seal plate, and mix well. This will elude the DNA from the beads (total 40 µL). Wait at least 5 minutes. ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[{"style":"sub","offset":28,"length":1}],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"fmcqe","text":"Centrifuge plate briefly. Place plate back onto the magnetic rack and wait for liquid to become clear (indicating the beads have bound to the magnet leaving your DNA in suspension). Transfer the suspension (30 µL is enough) to a new plate, leaving all the beads behind. This is your clean DNA that will be used in the next step. ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"9136d","text":"You will have picked up the indexing primers from Stephen Wilcox at WEHI. He provides 5 µL at 100 uM of each primer. You will want to dilute those to 5 uM by adding 45 µL of nuclease free H2O to each well. Mix well and centrifuge before moving on to the next step. You should preplan by creating a spreadsheet with all your samples and primer combinations.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[{"style":"sub","offset":189,"length":1}],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"aqo4l","text":"Add 1 μL of Fwd indexing primer (5 uM) to each well. Each row on a given plate will have the same Fwd primer. ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"95dbh","text":"Add 1 μL of Rev indexing primer (5 uM) to each well. Each column on a given plate will have the same Rev primer.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}
{"blocks":[{"key":"djcbp","text":"From Step 14 above, transfer 10 µL of clean DNA.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"51rfl","text":"Add 10 µL of MyTaq HS Red Mix. Seal, mix and centrifuge plate, then run the OH_24 program. ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"1j20k","text":"","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"2cjnr","text":"MyTaq polymerase Indexing PCR settings: 1 cycle × 95°C for 3 min; 24 cycles × 95°C for 15 s, 60°C for 30 s, and 72°C for 30 s; 1 cycle × 72°C for 7 min; hold at 4°C","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[{"style":"bold","offset":66,"length":2}],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"1corr","text":"","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"6tc8m","text":"On an agarose gel, run some random samples* from each plate to confirm correct sized bands","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"1ksqh","text":"with minimal non-specific bands. Run a few random samples representing each primer pair. The","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"cq44a","text":"expected size will depend on original amplicon size.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"13m2t","text":"","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}},{"key":"fmire","text":"*I opt to run each sample on a 1% agarose gel as described in step 5.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"7ipl1","text":"Working with one plate at a time, take 5 µL from each sample including negative controls and place in a 25 mL reservoir. Mix pool with a 1 mL pipet. Transfer whole pool volume to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube. For all 96 wells, this will be 500 µL in total volume.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}
{"blocks":[{"key":"601f4","text":"Transfer 50 µL of pool to a new 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube. ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"3sq4","text":"Add 30 µL of NGS beads to 50 µL library pool; leave at RT for 5 min. ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"bfff4","text":"Put tube onto magnetic rack and wait until you can see beads attaching to the side of the wells.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"b9kef","text":"Carefully aspirate off supernatant – be careful not to disturb the beads.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}
{"blocks":[{"key":"2r06","text":"Carefully add 180 µL of 80% ethanol then remove to wash the beads. ","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}
{"blocks":[{"key":"1hi3q","text":"Repeat step 26.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"44ufd","text":"Using a P20 pipettor take care to remove as much of the remaining ethanol solution as possible without disturbing the pellet.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}
{"blocks":[{"key":"992pd","text":"Transfer tube to a rack, and let tube air dry.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"p3k5","text":"Add 105 µL of nuclease free water and gently mix using a vortexer. Briefly spin.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}

{"blocks":[{"key":"m3qt","text":"Leave for 5 minutes and then place on magnetic rack. Once beads have migrated to magnet, transfer 90 µL to new 1.5 mL Eppendorf. This is your clean library pool. For each plate, transfer 20 µL to a new tube and place those tubes in a 50 mL falcon tube labeled with your contact information and sequencing details. The falcon tube will then be walked over to WEHI for sequencing on a single Illumina MiSeq run using v3 (2 × 300 bp) reagents. Prior to sequencing, each pool is run on the TapeStation to determine DNA concentration and the pools are normalized prior to loading on the MiSeq.","type":"unstyled","depth":0,"inlineStyleRanges":[],"entityRanges":[],"data":{}}],"entityMap":{}}
